23.heading: Geshur:
refs: Kenath was situated in the tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan. Eusebius says it was called in his time Καναθα, Kanatha
and was a town in the Trachonitis, near Bozra. Josephus places it in Coelo-syria
and Pliny reckons it among the cities of the Decapolis. It was also called Nobah, after Nobah an Israelite, who conquered it - Num 32:42
which is placed by Eusebius, eight miles south of Heshbon. see note on Judg 8:11 .
23.body:
Josh 13:13
2Sa 13:38
Kenath:
Kenath was situated in the tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan. Eusebius says it was called in his time Καναθα, Kanatha; and was a town in the Trachonitis, near Bozra. Josephus places it in Coelo-syria; and Pliny reckons it among the cities of the Decapolis. It was also called Nobah, after Nobah an Israelite, who conquered it - Num 32:42 ; which is placed by Eusebius, eight miles south of Heshbon. see note on Judg 8:11 .

35.heading: Sheshan:
refs: When the people of the East have no sons, they frequently marry their daughters to their slaves, even when they have much property to bestow upon them. Hassan had been the slave of Kamel, his predecessor

but Kamel, according to the custom of the country, gave him one of his daughters in marriage, and left him at his death one part of his great riches which he had amassed in the course of a long and prosperous life (Maillet, Lett. xi. p. 118).
1. Son of Jarha, father of Nathan 1Ch 2:35-36
2. One who came to David to Ziklan 1Ch 12:11
35.body:
When the people of the East have no sons, they frequently marry their daughters to their slaves, even when they have much property to bestow upon them.
